title: Geometry - Lesson 7 Practice: Triangle Congruence Postulates
description: Practice identifying SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, HL, and invalid triangle congruence shortcuts.

questions.question: Two triangles have all three pairs of corresponding sides congruent. Which reason proves the triangles congruent?
questions.explanation: Three congruent side pairs prove triangle congruence by SSS.

questions.question: Two triangles have two pairs of congruent sides and the included angle congruent. Which reason applies?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the angle between them prove congruence by SAS.

questions.question: AAA is enough to prove that two triangles are congruent.
questions.explanation: AAA proves the same shape, but the triangles may be different sizes, so it does not prove congruence.

questions.question: Which condition is required before using HL?
options: Both triangles must be right triangles.
The included angle must be obtuse.
questions.explanation: HL is a right triangle congruence theorem, so both triangles must be right triangles.

questions.question: Two angles and a non-included side prove triangle congruence by ______.
questions.explanation: AAS uses two congruent angle pairs and a side that is not between those angles.

questions.question: Given $\angle A \cong \angle D$, $\angle B \cong \angle E$, and $AB \cong DE$, which reason proves $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$?
questions.explanation: Side $AB$ is included between $\angle A$ and $\angle B$, and side $DE$ is included between $\angle D$ and $\angle E$, so the reason is ASA.

questions.question: Explain why SSA is not the same as SAS.
questions.correctAnswer: SAS uses the included angle between two congruent sides. SSA uses a non-included angle, which may not force one unique triangle.
questions.explanation: The position of the angle matters. In SAS the included angle locks the two side lengths into one triangle; in SSA it may not.

questions.question: In $\triangle PQR \cong \triangle XYZ$, which side corresponds to $\overline{QR}$? Explain how you know.
questions.correctAnswer: $\overline{YZ}$ corresponds to $\overline{QR}$ because the vertex order matches $P$ with $X$, $Q$ with $Y$, and $R$ with $Z$.
questions.explanation: Use the order of the congruence statement to match vertices and then match sides.
